body:
Just had this happen with Nvim's LSP via omni-completion on v0.7.0-dev+886-ga88046fe2, so this is indeed not limited to vim-lsp or `<C-n>`, `<C-p>` completion, though it seems to be less common.

Unfortunately, again, I was using a RelWithDebInfo build...

body: Apparently tagstackidx _is_ allowed to be equal to the tagstacklen.  This is weird and would need more time to dig into than my current drive-by.

If `w_tagstackidx == w_tagstacklen` is OK, then we must need the invariant `w_tagstacklen < TAGSTACKSIZE`. However, if you look at the `tagstack_push_item` implementation and suppose that `w_tagstacklen == TAGSTACKSIZE - 1`, it is easy to see that you'll end up with `w_tagstacklen == TAGSTACKSIZE`.

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/57a296d899d170e7f78aec2225bf8ab2b0dc711c/src/nvim/tag.c#L3355-L3363

Blame shows the relevant code hasn't been touched in 3 years. Maybe a more recent change (in a plugin?) is causing it to be hit more now. I'm hitting this once every day or two recently.

After looking more closely, it seems like most of the code is OK with `w_tagstackidx == TAGSTACKSIZE` and verifies that `w_tagstackidx < w_tagstacklen` before using it to index into the stack. One exception is in the opening lines of `find_tagfunc_tags` (which is near the top of the stack trace in https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/15221#issuecomment-1013800627)

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/57a296d899d170e7f78aec2225bf8ab2b0dc711c/src/nvim/tag.c#L1136-L1146

body:
I found a consistent way to reproduce:

* use clangd lsp plugin
* use go-to-definition. this will add a tag to the stack
* repeat 20 times to get a full tag stack (verify using `:tags`)
* use completion
* crash
